sessions.title: Design, Simulate, Ship: End-to-End AI Agents on Connect Customer
sessions.desc: Most AI agent projects stall between pilot and production. In this workshop, you go from an idea to a production-ready agentic customer experience in a single session using Amazon Connect Customer. No months-long timeline.

sessions.title: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
sessions.desc: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

sessions.title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.desc: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

sessions.title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
sessions.desc: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

sessions.title: Getting Started with AgentCore: ship an agent to production in 3 hours
sessions.desc: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. Not because the AI is hard, but because the infrastructure around it is: memory, tool access, identity, policy, observability, evaluation. This workshop closes that gap in three hours. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add each production capability using the AgentCore CLI: runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy, observability, and evaluation. AgentCore is framework and model agnostic, so everything applies whether you use LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own stack. Leave ready to ship.

sessions.title: Cloud Migration Journey Tabletop Experience
sessions.desc: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture.

sessions.title: Ontology-Powered AI Agents: Verifiable Decisions Across Manufacturing
sessions.desc: Manufacturing stakeholders make dozens of high-velocity decisions daily. Each must be traceable, defensible, and grounded in enterprise knowledge and lifecycle data. Yet the systems informing these decisions remain siloed, and AI agents reasoning over this fragmented data cannot produce verifiable results. Ontologies solve this by structuring manufacturing knowledge so agents can trace decisions back to their source data. In this chalk talk, we show how ontology-grounded agents, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, make verifiable decisions across the lifecycle with a live demo. Attendees leave with a reference architecture, best practices, and a clear path to building verifiable AI agents for manufacturing.

sessions.title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
sessions.desc: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.

sessions.title: Data Mesh to Agentic AI: Building an AI-Ready Enterprise on AWS
sessions.desc: How do you build an AI-ready data foundation in a global investment organization without compromising trust, governance, or speed? CPP Investments—manager of one of the world’s largest pension funds—is evolving from fragmented data toward a governed enterprise data platform on AWS, using data mesh principles, federated ownership, and platform engineering to scale with guardrails. Join their CTO for a look inside the architecture, operating model, and critical trade-offs shaping this evolution, and how it brings trusted data closer to investment decisions while laying the foundation for conversational data experiences and agentic AI.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

sessions.title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
sessions.desc: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

sessions.title: Building Smarter Self-Service Experiences with AI
sessions.desc: Great customer self-service starts with the knowledge your team already has, but getting it into customers' hands can be a challenge. In this builder session, explore how AI can help you transform existing resources into live self-service experiences quickly and easily. Learn how teams are reducing time-to-launch without heavy engineering lifts.
sessions.room: MGM Grand, Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: End-to-end resilience for your cloud workloads
sessions.desc: In this session, learn how to continuously assess and validate the operational resilience of your end-to-end business services using AWS Resilience Hub. See how GenAI agents automatically discover and map your application dependencies to give you a holistic picture of your resilience posture. Get actionable recommendations to close gaps, generate regulatory compliance artifacts to meet your compliance needs, and put it all to the test with end-to-end resilience testing to prove it.
sessions.room: Caesars Forum, Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater

sessions.title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
sessions.desc: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

sessions.title: Best practices for AI powered software development on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.desc: You already have a preferred coding agent for software development. That agent touches your codebase, your infrastructure, and your production environment, and it needs guardrails, permissions, and rules to operate safely. In this workshop you connect an agent of your choice, such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, to Amazon Bedrock and deliver a real application from brief to production. You define specs the agent can act on, wire in automated test gates, apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and lock down permissions before anything reaches infrastructure. Leave with a working app and a repeatable architecture you can adopt immediately. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
sessions.desc: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.
speakers: Senior Developer Relations Engineer / AWS Serverless Hero
sessions.room: Caesars Forum, Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk

sessions.title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
sessions.desc: Raise the bar on your software supply chain security with AWS. In this chalk talk, we will discuss DevOps security best-practices, threat detection and incident response for containers, and how to leverage AWS security services including Amazon ECR, Amazon GuardDuty, and Amazon Inspector to protect your Amazon EKS workloads. Discover how you can ensure CVE patching while optimizing storage to accelerate image delivery through seamless integration with open-source tools for publishing and deploying containerized workloads at scale. Learn how to efficently streamline your software supply chain while mitigating risks.

sessions.title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
sessions.desc: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

sessions.title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
sessions.desc: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

sessions.title: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
sessions.desc: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
sessions.desc: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

sessions.title: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
sessions.desc: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Promenade Level, Pompeian IV

sessions.title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
sessions.desc: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.
speakers: Sr. Manager, AWS Sustainability - Science, Services, Infrastructure, and Innovation

sessions.title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
sessions.desc:
Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to.
Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
sessions.desc: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom I

sessions.title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
sessions.desc: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

sessions.title: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
sessions.desc: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom III

sessions.title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
sessions.desc:
Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately.

Bring your laptop to participate.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1

sessions.title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
sessions.desc: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

sessions.title: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
sessions.desc: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.
sessions.room: Caesars Forum, Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk

sessions.title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
sessions.desc: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: 3rd Party Risk Management Tabletop Experience
sessions.desc: Embark on "Third Party Risk Management," an engaging tabletop designed to challenge and refine your approach to managing external partnerships and vendor relationships. In this immersive experience, leaders are thrust into a high-stakes environment where they must navigate complex scenarios involving third-party risks. This tabletop not only enhances your ability to manage third-party risks effectively but also equips you with practical insights and strategies to safeguard your organization’s interests and strengthen its external partnerships. Join us to elevate your risk management acumen and drive resilient, forward-thinking approaches in an interconnected business landscape.

sessions.title: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
sessions.desc: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Then extend it — encode your team's expertise as skills, connect custom MCP tools, automate investigations from alarms, and approve agent-executed fixes. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

sessions.title: Deploy infrastructure with speed and safety using AWS CloudFormation
sessions.desc: In this workshop, build and test AWS CloudFormation templates hands-on. Create stacks to deploy and manage resources, then use the CloudFormation Language Server to author with real-time validation in your IDE. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
sessions.desc: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.title: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
sessions.desc: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation. In this chalk talk, we'll explore when to use first-party tools, when AWS Lambda gives you more flexibility, and when MCP integrations make sense—with latency, operational complexity, and compliance requirements as the deciding factors. We’ll discuss patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI agents and automated evaluation pipelines using Contact Lens and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. You'll leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center, including guidance for financial services and regulated industries.

sessions.title: Executive Night at the Sphere
sessions.desc: TBD

sessions.title: AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC)
sessions.desc: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) reimagines how teams plan, build, and ship software with AI as a first-class participant. In this bootcamp, learn the three phases (Inception, Construction, Operation) , apply the Intent-Unit-Bolt framework to decompose requirements into AI-executable work items, then use Kiro IDE's Spec-Driven Development to generate domain models, application code, tests, and infrastructure. You leave with a working application built entirely through the AI-DLC methodology.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom I

sessions.title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
sessions.desc:
Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why.

Bring your laptop to participate.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1

sessions.title: Enhanced container image access & distribution with Amazon ECR
sessions.desc: Amazon ECR is trusted by millions to store and serve container images, but the way teams discover, trust, and consume container software is evolving fast. In this session, the ECR product team shares where container distribution on AWS is heading: making it easier to find the software you need, trust what you run, acquire it simply, and pull it privately and securely inside your own environment. Through practical examples, we'll explore new capabilities that help publishers reach customers at scale and help organizations govern and consume containers with confidence. Whether you publish container software or run it in production, you'll leave with a clear picture of how ECR is becoming the center of the container software supply chain.

sessions.title: Defense-in-Depth for Containers on Amazon EKS: A Layering Story
sessions.desc: On a default Amazon EKS cluster, a single pod is a compromise away from the whole cluster - shared node credentials, flat networking, implicit trust, open egress. In this code-first session we start there, then trace how EKS security grew layer by layer as the threat model matured. We rebuild an over-privileged workload live, adding one control at a time: scoped pod identity, admin and DNS network policies, and private certificate trust with zero-downtime CA rotation. We finish by running a lateral-movement attempt against the hardened workload and watching it fail at multiple layers — the whole point of defense-in-depth.

sessions.title: Evaluate, select, optimize and find your best model
sessions.desc: Most teams pick a model on instinct. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build a structured evaluation pipeline for your own use case, run it against multiple model candidates (frontier and open-weight), and learn exactly when customization is worth the investment vs. when prompt engineering or RAG is enough. You'll leave with a working evaluation harness, a decision framework for technique selection (SFT vs. RFT vs. CPT), and a trained model you can take home.

sessions.title: Build agentic AI applications with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS
sessions.desc: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

sessions.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Tabletop Experience
sessions.desc: Quantum computing is advancing—is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence. Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

sessions.title: Never Start Over: Chat to Co-Browse, Voice and Video on Amazon Connect Customer
sessions.desc: Your customer is halfway through an application in your app, and stuck. Today they abandon it, call you, and start explaining from scratch. In this hands-on workshop you build a single unbroken conversation that escalates in richness without losing context. A customer opens chat inside your application. When they stall on a form, the agent co-browses the page and sees the blocking field, then uses agent assist to answer a policy question with cited sources. The conversation carries into an in-app call, context intact, no phone number and no repeated details. Documents are reviewed over screen share, identity is confirmed over video, and because it's a joint application the co-applicant and a product specialist join the same call. Walk away with an escalation pattern combining persistent context, WebRTC channels and AI-assisted agents, for any high-consideration interaction.

sessions.title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Building an AI-Ready Data Foundation
sessions.desc: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
sessions.desc: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Promenade Level, Milano IV

sessions.title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
sessions.desc: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.

sessions.title: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
sessions.desc: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

sessions.title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
sessions.desc: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.

sessions.title: Spec-Driven AI Development with Kiro
sessions.desc: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) brings structure, traceability, and human oversight to every phase of high-velocity, Agentic-AI powered software delivery. In this bootcamp, apply AI-DLC in Kiro to build a production application through Feature Specs, control agent behavior with steering files and execution modes, extend capabilities with MCP servers and Kiro Powers, and automate workflows with hooks. Leave with a governed, repeatable process for shipping quality software with AI assistance.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom I

sessions.title: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.desc: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: Scaling legacy app modernization with autonomous agents
sessions.desc: Legacy application modernization is a coordination and code generation problem. A large application must be understood, verified, and integrated without losing fidelity. AWS Transform for mainframe reads legacy code and extracts its business rules into traceable specifications that describe what the application does. Learn how AWS Transform overcomes this modernization challenge, and discover the latest capabilities for scaling modernization that compress delivery from days to hours.
sessions.room: Caesars Forum, Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater

sessions.title: Monetizing your applications with AWS
sessions.desc: In this session, learn how to transform your finished application into a revenue-generating SaaS product. Learn about analyzing your cloud infrastructure, choose pricing models, and instrumenting code for usage metering. You'll see how to manage the complete billing lifecycle, from subscription management and invoicing to tax calculation and payment processing. Walk away with a clear path to accelerate your time-to-market and start charging customers.

sessions.title: Never Start Over: Chat to Co-Browse, Voice and Video on Amazon Connect Customer
sessions.desc: Your customer is halfway through an application in your app, and stuck. Today they abandon it, call you, and start explaining from scratch. In this hands-on workshop you build a single unbroken conversation that escalates in richness without losing context. A customer opens chat inside your application. When they stall on a form, the agent co-browses the page and sees the blocking field, then uses agent assist to answer a policy question with cited sources. The conversation carries into an in-app call, context intact, no phone number and no repeated details. Documents are reviewed over screen share, identity is confirmed over video, and because it's a joint application the co-applicant and a product specialist join the same call. Walk away with an escalation pattern combining persistent context, WebRTC channels and AI-assisted agents, for any high-consideration interaction.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Promenade Level, Pompeian IV

sessions.title: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
sessions.desc: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
sessions.desc: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
sessions.desc: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

sessions.title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
sessions.desc: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
sessions.desc: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build real-time applications with AWS Amplify
sessions.desc: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
sessions.desc: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent, progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll create a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.
speakers: Worldwide Specialist Solution Architect HCLS – Data & AI/ML

sessions.title: Assume breach, prove recovery: a ransomware resilience workshop
sessions.desc: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

sessions.title: Observability and operations in the AI era
sessions.desc: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

sessions.title: Getting Started with AgentCore: ship an agent to production in 3 hours
sessions.desc: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. Not because the AI is hard, but because the infrastructure around it is: memory, tool access, identity, policy, observability, evaluation. This workshop closes that gap in three hours. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add each production capability using the AgentCore CLI: runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy, observability, and evaluation. AgentCore is framework and model agnostic, so everything applies whether you use LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own stack. Leave ready to ship.

sessions.title: Deploy infrastructure with speed and safety using AWS CloudFormation
sessions.desc: In this workshop, build and test AWS CloudFormation templates hands-on. Create stacks to deploy and manage resources, then use the CloudFormation Language Server to author with real-time validation in your IDE. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
sessions.desc: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. speakers: Worldwide Specialist Solution Architect HCLS – Data & AI/ML

sessions.title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
sessions.desc: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom I

sessions.title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
sessions.desc: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

sessions.title: Monitor AI workloads and agents end to end
sessions.desc: Get hands-on with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, the next evolution of CloudWatch that converges application and agent observability into one AI-powered solution. Instrument an agent, trace its execution, run evaluations, and experiment with prompts and models in your IDE. Explore auto-discovered topology, golden metrics, and AI-powered investigation with AWS DevOps Agent.

sessions.title: How Elevance Health Delivers an AI-Native Member Experience on Real-Time Context
sessions.desc: Members shouldn't have to navigate fragmented systems to understand their benefits and find the right care. Rather than solving one interaction at a time, Elevance Health designed for the holistic member experience. Serving 46 million members, they are building a real-time context layer that unifies clinical, claims, and behavioral data to power AI agents that deliver personalized guidance across the entire care journey. Amazon Connect Customer consumes this context at the point of interaction, enabling associates and AI agents to anticipate needs, surface relevant information, and trigger next-best-actions. Attendees will learn how semantic data layers and agentic workflows come together under a governed deployment model for regulated healthcare.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater

sessions.title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
sessions.desc: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

sessions.title: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
sessions.desc: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building event-driven architectures
sessions.desc: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
sessions.desc: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
sessions.desc: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

sessions.title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
sessions.desc: Your application works perfectly in the lab, but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.
sessions.room: MGM Grand, Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: Graviton5 for data workloads
sessions.desc: Data workloads are bottlenecked by how fast they can access and process information — whether that data lives on local storage, in memory, or behind a lightweight service. New Graviton5 instance families are purpose-built for each tier.

sessions.title: Diagnose Complex Workloads with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.desc: Follow an investigation of a complex workload using AWS DevOps Agent. Trace an application-level symptom through multiple layers of your environment across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. See how DevOps Agent analyzes telemetry, correlates signals across layers, identifies likely root causes, and delivers targeted remediation. Learn practical techniques for investigating workloads and reducing the manual effort of diagnosing problems across distributed environments.

sessions.title: Resolve Incidents and Validate Releases with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.desc: Follow an issue from detection to resolution. In this builder's session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates incidents across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Then use the AWS DevOps Agent release management agent to review the code changes for production readiness before they reach your customers. Every review is informed by production intelligence that AWS DevOps Agent continuously builds from your environment.

sessions.title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
sessions.desc: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.

sessions.title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
sessions.desc:
Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
sessions.desc: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Then extend it — encode your team's expertise as skills, connect custom MCP tools, automate investigations from alarms, and approve agent-executed fixes. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

sessions.title: Innovations in DNS and Amazon Route 53
sessions.desc: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in Domain Name Systems (DNS) and Amazon Route 53. This session covers new capabilities in DNS resolution and new approaches to private and public domain resolution. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify DNS at scale.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Build agentic AI applications with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS
sessions.desc: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

sessions.title: From Legacy to Agentic: Modernization Beyond the Code (sponsored by SoftServe)

Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.
sessions.room: Venetian, Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

sessions.title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
sessions.desc: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

sessions.title: Become an AWS AI Business Strategist
sessions.desc: Turning an AI idea into enterprise reality requires more than technical knowledge. In this bootcamp, you apply the Discover, Design, Deliver framework to diagnose business problems, assess organizational readiness, and scope AI pilots with clear success criteria. You navigate responsible AI tradeoffs, lead change management across cross-functional teams, evaluate agentic AI architectures for autonomy versus control, and build phased scaling strategies from proof of concept through production deployment.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Emperors Level, Augustus Ballroom I

sessions.title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
sessions.desc: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

sessions.title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
sessions.desc: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.title: Building Interactive Web Applications on AWS Lambda
sessions.desc: If you're running Express, Hono, or Fastify on traditional serverless compute today, you're wrapping your HTTP server in an event-handler adapter and working around single-concurrency execution. In this session, see how AWS Lambda is evolving to support web workloads natively. Come see what's next for web developers on serverless.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Promenade Level, Roman I

sessions.title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
sessions.desc: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.
sessions.room: Caesars Palace, Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Code Talk

sessions.title: Build an AI agent that understands customer intent
sessions.desc: Today's AI agents start every session cold. They don't know what the customer was just browsing, whether they're frustrated or exploring, or whether this is a service moment or a buying moment. So they waste the first few turns asking what your data already knows. In this hands-on builders' session, you close that gap. You unify customer data into Profiles, then turn it into real-time signals about what each customer needs. You wire those signals into an AI agent with calculated attributes and event triggers, so when the customer makes contact the agent already understands why they're there and responds with the right answer and the right offer. You leave with a working prototype ready for your own environment.
sessions.room: MGM Grand, Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

sessions.title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS
sessions.desc: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

sessions.title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS

You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

sessions.title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
sessions.desc:
AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards.

sessions.title: Cloud Migration Journey Tabletop Experience

sessions.title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
sessions.desc: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

sessions.title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
sessions.desc: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

sessions.title: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless

Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Give AI Agents Business Context with Genie One and Genie Ontology (sponsored by Databricks)

See how Genie One uses this shared context to reason over live structured and unstructured data, call tools through MCP, take action and deliver more accurate results with less costly agentic exploration on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.
sessions.room: Venetian, Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

sessions.title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent

AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.

sessions.title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
