sessions.desc: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Deploying Governed AI Agents in Clinical AI
sessions.desc: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. Radiology Partners is tackling this with MosaicOS, a full imaging lifecycle system powered by agentic AI that spans order placement through billing. In this lightning talk, learn how MosaicOS uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate multiple AI models across the radiology workflow while maintaining governance and observability required in regulated clinical environments. See how agentic orchestration moves radiology from tool-level automation to coordinated, clinician-directed intelligence at scale.
sessions.room: Venetian, Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

sessions.title: 5 Questions Terraform, OpenTofu, and CloudFormation Can't Answer (sponsored by Spacelift, Inc.)
sessions.desc: Every infrastructure change is one run: code, an engine, a plan, an apply. That run is still a wall of unstructured log text, and the questions about your estate go unanswered. Five to ask of your IaC: Did Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, or Ansible run it, and does it matter? Where does the time go, and can OpenTelemetry tracing show you? What happens outside the engine: providers, state, policy-as-code, drift, queue time? What about unmanaged resources, the half of your AWS account no run ever touched? Who gets self-service, and can an AI agent be trusted with an apply? This presentation is brought to you by Spacelift, Inc., an AWS Partner.
sessions.room: Venetian, Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

sessions.title: Public Sector Reception
sessions.desc: You're invited to the AWS re:Invent Public Sector Party. Unwind and connect with mission-driven peers and AWS experts who understand the unique challenges - and opportunities - of the public sector. Join us for an evening of great conversation and connection as we celebrate the impact of cloud innovation in service of the public good. Enjoy an evening of networking and meet the people driving change across government, education, and nonprofits to toast what's ahead.
sessions.room: Marquee Nightclub at The Cosmopolitan Hotel

sessions.title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
sessions.desc: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

sessions.title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
sessions.desc: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: 3rd Party Risk Management Tabletop Experience
sessions.desc: Embark on "Third Party Risk Management," an engaging tabletop designed to challenge and refine your approach to managing external partnerships and vendor relationships. In this immersive experience, leaders are thrust into a high-stakes environment where they must navigate complex scenarios involving third-party risks. This tabletop not only enhances your ability to manage third-party risks effectively but also equips you with practical insights and strategies to safeguard your organization’s interests and strengthen its external partnerships. Join us to elevate your risk management acumen and drive resilient, forward-thinking approaches in an interconnected business landscape.

sessions.title: Building event-driven architectures
sessions.desc: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
sessions.desc: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.
sessions.room: MGM Grand, Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater

sessions.title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
sessions.desc: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

sessions.title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
sessions.desc: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.
speakers: Director, Amazon ElastiCache, Neptune, and Timestream
Head of Product, ElastiCache, Neptune, and MemoryDB
sessions.room: Caesars Forum, Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater

sessions.title: AWS Backup: Architecture deep dive
sessions.desc: Dive into AWS Backup architecture with AWS experts, including how new capabilities fit into your design. We work through deployment strategies, backup storage options, restore scenarios, and security posture. Bring your questions, leave with a plan.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 Tables: A deep dive into storage built for Apache Iceberg
sessions.desc: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.
sessions.room: MGM Grand, Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater

sessions.title: Build agentic observability workflows with AI tools from AWS Marketplace
sessions.desc: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.desc: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

sessions.title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
sessions.desc: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

sessions.title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
sessions.desc: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless
sessions.desc: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, discover how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services—from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Tabletop Experience
sessions.desc: Quantum computing is advancing—is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence. Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

sessions.title: AI innovations across network monitoring and operations
sessions.desc: Join us to explore how AI is transforming network monitoring and observability. This session dives into new capabilities for traffic analysis, network health monitoring, and faster issue resolution that shows how intelligent, automated tooling helps you move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive insight. Whether you want to cut time-to-resolution or get a clearer, real-time pulse on your network's health, come see what's new and what's on the horizon.

sessions.title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
sessions.desc: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

sessions.title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
sessions.desc:
AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
sessions.desc: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

sessions.title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
sessions.desc: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

sessions.title: Processing PII without exposing it: KYC with Nitro Enclaves
sessions.desc: Know Your Customer (KYC) pipelines must screen personally identifiable informaiton (PII) against sanctions lists and politically exposed person (PEP) databases while proving to regulators that data was never exposed to unauthorized systems. Traditional Spark pipelines may give executors access to decrypted PII, creating compliance risk. In this workshop, learn how to combine AWS Nitro Enclaves with Amazon EMR on EKS to process PII at scale without exposing plaintext to the compute layer. You'll configure KMS key policies with PCR0 attestation, deploy enclave sidecars as Kubernetes DaemonSets, and run Spark jobs where only screening decisions leave the enclave boundary.
speakers: Amazon Web Services India Private Limited

sessions.title: Orchestrate GuardDuty and Network Firewall to prevent exfiltration
sessions.desc: Compromised workloads and AI agents share a common path: outbound channels that most teams barely monitor. From CVE-driven RCE on EC2 to prompt injection on agentic systems, both threats end with unauthorized data leaving your environment. In this session, dive deep into a layered egress architecture combining AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoint policies, SCPs, RCPs, GuardDuty, and IAM Access Analyzer. We'll trace concrete attack scenarios through each control and show how to orchestrate them to prevent data exfiltration.

sessions.title: Build your iOS CI/CD pipeline with AI agents on EC2 Mac
sessions.desc: Build iOS CI/CD pipelines on Amazon EC2 Mac using AI-powered workflows with Kiro CLI and AWS MCP Server. Define infrastructure as declarative specs while AI agents guide deployment, explain concepts, and validate configurations. This hands-on workshop covers EC2 Mac architecture, dedicated hosts, Xcode automation, GitLab setup, and CloudWatch monitoring through interactive AI modules. Learn to collaborate with agents and balance automation with understanding. Gain practical experience in both EC2 Mac operations and modern spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflows for Apple platforms.

sessions.title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
sessions.desc: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.
sessions.room: Wynn/Encore, Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk

sessions.title: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.desc: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.

sessions.title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
sessions.desc: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.
